column2: Quartermasters will connect aid stations to transport and rest facilities. After the split, Shabrat's units will recover organisation faster between battles. The prepared network will remain with the resistance.
Disrupted Capital Command
The attack on the capital's apparatus disrupted the Party headquarters. Commanders are restoring control over their units and coordinating their plans.
Underground Combat Cells

We will combine the industrial and capital underground's contacts into a network of combat cells. After the split, Shabrat will be able to fund operations against Party territorial brigades. The network's capacity is limited: no more than three formations can be destroyed during the civil war.

After the split, Shabrat's army will receive decisions targeting Party territorial brigades in Stelander's districts. An operation costing £political_power_texticon §Y35§! and £ADISCORD_economy_treasury_texticon §Y1200§! takes §Y21 days§! and destroys §Yone§! brigade present in the selected district. Only one operation can run at a time; successful operations must begin at least §Y45 days§! apart, with a maximum of §Ythree§! during the war. Losing the target or ending the war refunds the entire payment.
Underground Strike against the Garrison: [FROM.GetName]

Combat cells will eliminate one Party territorial brigade in the selected district. After 21 days, the formation will be destroyed along with its personnel and equipment. Allied, foreign and other division types are not valid targets. If no suitable brigade remains, the district changes controller or the war ends, the operation is cancelled with a full refund. No more than three operations can be completed successfully during the war.
Shabrat is at war with the Party; neither side has capitulated; fewer than three operations have succeeded
No other paid strike is active; 45 days have elapsed since the previous successful operation began

A Unified State Treasury

The civil war ended before the accountants could establish what state remained after it. District coffers, factory ledgers and tax books must once again describe one country rather than several military administrations.
Revenue and expenditure will be recalculated across the reunified territory. Reforms accumulate in the post-war republic's national spirit.
The Republic's Tax Service

During the war, collectors disappeared along with the archives, and enterprises paid whoever controlled the nearest road. The new government must restore a unified taxpayer register and separate taxation from field levies.
A unified taxpayer register turns wartime levies into steady state revenue.
Restart Civilian Workshops
Repair shops that were patching up trucks and rifles yesterday can once again manufacture equipment for mines, roads and homes. State orders must return them to civilian work.
A civilian factory is built in an owned, controlled Stelandic region with available space. If no suitable region exists, the treasury receives §G900§! instead.
Monetary Stabilisation

After months of military IOUs, emergency purchases and separate coffers, the value of money has become a political question. The Council of Ministers and the banks must agree on which obligations the republic recognises and how it will honour them.
Inflation: §G-8§! percentage points. Deficit pressure: §G-10§! percentage points. Neither can fall below zero.
The First Development Budget

Reconstruction will no longer be a series of emergency payments. Roads, civilian industry, local administrations and debt will receive a shared budget planned for several years rather than the coming week.
Steady revenue, expenditure management and civilian production are brought together in a long-term reconstruction programme.
The Country Must Live

Victory explains who gained power, but not why people should build schools, workshops and roads again. State propaganda must exchange the language of the front for the language of reconstruction: Steland exists not for the next war, but for the life that follows it.
Growth across all national development dimensions: §G+5%§!.
Posters on the Ruins

The walls still bear the marks of shellfire, and that is where the new campaign's first posters will appear. Districts will compete not in numbers of volunteers, but in reopened schools, functioning services and restored streets.
Monthly society growth: §G+1§!. Monthly state development growth: §G+1§!. Society development growth: §G+5%§!.
Reconstruction as a Duty

The republic will declare reconstruction a civic duty, just as district defence was until recently. Engineers, workers and local administrations will be recognised as participants in a common state project.
Monthly economic development growth: §G+1§!. Economic development growth: §G+7%§!. Construction speed: §G+5%§!.
Engineers on the Air
Instead of endless speeches about enemies, radio will feature the people restoring power grids, bridges, hospitals and production. Competence must become part of the new state's public image.
Monthly state development growth: §G+1§!. State development growth: §G+7%§!. Research speed: §G+3%§!.
The Reconstruction Generation

If war shaped a generation of the front, peace must shape a generation of reconstruction. Schools, the press and state programmes will tie personal success to national growth rather than membership in another armed group.
Monthly society, state and economic growth: §G+1§! in each dimension. Growth across all development dimensions: §G+8%§!. Additional society, state and economic growth: §G+5%§!.
Reopen the Universities

Military headquarters took the best lecturers, laboratories lost equipment, and some institutes existed only on paper for years. The state will return funding, premises and the ability to plan beyond the next campaigning season to the universities.
Adds §G1 permanent research slot§!. Research speed: §G+2%§!.
National Research Institutes

Restored universities alone are not enough. The republic will establish a network of specialised institutes linked to industry, infrastructure and state planning. Science must become a permanent national function rather than a peacetime luxury.
Adds another §G1 permanent research slot§!. Research speed: §G+3%§!. Economic and state development growth: §G+3%§!.
The First Reconstruction Plan

Victory ended the civil war, but did not restore normal life. The government must rebuild the economy, restore trust in the centre and persuade the districts to function once more as parts of a single state.

Emergency Reconstruction Teams
Direct treasury funds towards bridges, substations, railway junctions and damaged workshops. Within weeks, these teams must show that the central government knows how to repair as well as mobilise.
District Administration Congresses

Bring officials, municipal councils and military commandants together for a series of district meetings. The centre will receive a list of real problems, and the regions a channel of influence that does not run through armed headquarters.
Publish the Wartime Accounts
Disclose some of the emergency expenditure, requisition lists and wartime debts. It will be painful for the cabinet, but silence about missing money destroys trust faster than any figures.
Housing for Demobilised Soldiers
Convert empty barracks, allocate construction materials and subsidise housing for families returning from the front. The war must have a visible end.
Complete the First Reconstruction Plan

Essential services are functioning, the districts have rejoined a common administrative system, and society no longer lives in anticipation of another mobilisation. The first emergency phase can end, allowing a transition to long-term development.
Reconstruction Propaganda

After the civil war, propaganda must compete for attention just as construction and administrative programmes compete for money. The number of simultaneous campaigns is limited by the available propaganda slots.
'A Country Rebuilt'
Posters, newsreels and local newspapers show road repairs, workshops opening and public services being restored instead of leaders on platforms.
'One Steland'
The campaign stresses that the front lines disappeared along with the military administrations. Districts must once again see one another as parts of a single state.
